parameters.seeding: blake2b(asset:parameter) through _procgen_building._param_rng - keyed per parameter, so a parameter added later cannot re-roll what is already placed

convention.frame: glTF +Y up, +Z forward, +X right; origin at the footprint centre on the ground
convention.source: measured from assets/ready/longhouse, building_well and prop_iron_banded_oak_door, and stated in tools/asset_pipeline/_procgen_building.py's header
convention.units: metres, 1 unit = 1 m, no node scale

world_truth.note: 19 placements, each `circle_m: [x, z, 0.62]` with `height_m: 1.20`. The model is built to the box the shipped asset occupied - 1.9457 x 1.2000 x 0.9094 m, min [-0.9728, 0.0, -0.4547] - so none of the 19 moves and no content YAML was touched.

source_provenance.lod_policy: regrown per level at a coarser tessellation, not decimated off LOD0
source_provenance.textures: embedded in the GLB, resampled from the Cairnwold map sets: bark (cw_dead_wood, 2048 px source) at 2048 px and sawn END GRAIN (cw_log_end, 2048 px source, a 4x4 atlas of distinct cut faces) at 2048 px on LOD0, halved per level

collision.note: UNCHANGED AND DELIBERATELY SO: the collision hull is not rebuilt, so the 19 instances collide exactly as before

source_provenance.note: Stacked split firewood, 54 logs in six rows, 1.20 m high. Each log is a lobed round section swept along its own bent, tapering centreline with a sawn end at each face, so no two logs share a diameter, a length, a taper or a rotation - built to replace six-sided prisms, which is what the shipped asset was (54 hexagons, 8 distinct face normals in the whole model).
source_provenance.authored: parametric, exact dimensions in the world frame; generator tools/asset_pipeline/_procgen_woodpile.py, replacing G:/UNNAMED_DS_ASSETS/cairnwold/_build/build_cairnwold_village.py

reuses: _procgen_hurdle.tube (the lobed round section swept along a centreline, with cylindrical UVs and chamfered, radially-unwrapped cut ends)

not_reused.chamfered_box / chamfer_width: CHAMFER_SCALE defaults to 0, so chamfer_width returns 0.0 (measured by _procgen_hurdle); the 6 mm cut chamfer carries the number, not the call. A log is roundwood, so a chamfered box would read as sawn timber.
not_reused.build_cairnwold_village.woodpile: the asset being replaced, and it is the fault: six-sided prisms from acc.cyl(..., 6). Its STATUS header says its props are the region's weakest assets and must not be upgraded in that file's style.

source_provenance.licence_evidence: authored parametrically by tools/asset_pipeline/_procgen_woodpile.py. No third-party geometry is imported. Its textures are the Cairnwold material bank - cw_dead_wood is CC0 1.0 (Poly Haven dead_tree_trunk, LICENSE.txt in the pack) and cw_timber_beam is first-party/CC0 per its own record.
